subject: economics
question_text: How is food security ensured in India?
answer_text: Food security is ensured in a country when the three dimensions of food security are taken care of. The three dimensions are: Availability of food, Accessibility of food, and Affordability of food. Food security has been ensured in India because of self-sufficiency in food grains, a food-security system, implementation of poverty-alleviation programmes, and involvement of cooperatives and NGOs.
final_answer: Thus, food security in India is ensured through various measures addressing availability, accessibility, and affordability.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of food security dimensions and their implementation.

subject: economics
question_text: Which are the people more prone to food insecurity?
answer_text: The people more prone to food insecurity include landless and land-poor households, traditional artisans, ill-paid workers, backward sections of society, and those affected by natural disasters.
final_answer: Therefore, various socio-economic groups are more vulnerable to food insecurity.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of socio-economic factors affecting food security.

subject: economics
question_text: Which states are more food insecure in India?
answer_text: The economically-backward states with high incidence of poverty, such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, parts of Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra, are more food insecure in India.
final_answer: Thus, these states account for the largest number of food insecure people in the country.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires knowledge of regional disparities in food security.

subject: economics
question_text: Do you believe that Green Revolution has made India self-sufficient in food grains? How?
answer_text: Yes, the Green Revolution introduced high-yielding varieties of seeds, which, along with chemical fertilizers and pesticides, increased food grain productivity, helping India attain self-sufficiency in food grains.
final_answer: Therefore, the Green Revolution has significantly contributed to India's self-sufficiency in food grains.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding agricultural advancements and their impact.

subject: economics
question_text: A section of people in India are still without food. Explain.
answer_text: A large section of people in India suffers from food and nutrition insecurity, including landless agricultural laborers, casual laborers, and backward social sections. The government has implemented various schemes to ensure food security, but issues like mismanagement and dependency on monsoons still leave many without food.
final_answer: Thus, despite government efforts, food insecurity persists due to various systemic issues.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves multi-faceted understanding of food security issues.

subject: economics
question_text: What happens to the supply of food when there is a disaster or a calamity?
answer_text: When there is a disaster or a calamity, the production of food grains decreases in the affected area. This in turn creates a shortage of food in the area. Due to the food shortage, the prices go up. The raised prices of food materials affect the capacity of many people to buy the same. When the calamity occurs in a very wide spread area or is stretched over a long period of time, it may cause a situation of starvation. A massive starvation can take the form of famine.
final_answer: Thus, disasters lead to decreased food production, increased prices, and potential starvation.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding the impact of disasters on food supply and prices.

subject: economics
question_text: Differentiate between seasonal hunger and chronic hunger.
answer_text: Seasonal hunger is related to cycles of food growing and harvesting, prevalent in rural areas due to agricultural activities and in urban areas due to casual labor. Chronic hunger is a consequence of diets persistently inadequate in quantity and/or quality, affecting poor people who cannot afford food for survival.
final_answer: In summary, seasonal hunger is temporary and linked to agricultural cycles, while chronic hunger is a persistent issue due to inadequate income.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding and explaining two different types of hunger.

subject: economics
question_text: What has our government done to provide food security to the poor? Discuss any two schemes launched by the government?
answer_text: The government has ensured food security through a food-security system involving buffer stock maintenance and public distribution. Two schemes are: 1) Antyodaya Anna Yojana, which provides subsidized food grains to the poorest families, and 2) National Food for Work Programme, which offers wage employment to rural poor.
final_answer: Thus, the government has implemented various schemes to enhance food security for the poor.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires knowledge of government schemes and their impact on food security.

subject: economics
question_text: Why is a buffer stock created by the government?
answer_text: A buffer stock of food grains is created by the government to distribute procured food grains in food-deficit areas and among poorer sections at lower prices than the market price. It helps resolve food shortages during adverse conditions.
final_answer: Therefore, buffer stocks are essential for maintaining food security during shortages.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the purpose of buffer stocks in food security.

subject: Economics
question_text: Write a note on the role of cooperatives in providing food and related items.
answer_text: Along with the government, cooperatives are also playing an important role in ensuring food security in India, especially in the southern and western parts of the country. The cooperative societies set up shops to sell low-priced goods to the poor. Out of all fair-price shops running in Tamil Nadu, around 94 per cent are being run by cooperatives. Mother Dairy, in Delhi, is involved in providing milk and vegetables at controlled rates decided by the government. Amul, responsible for the White Revolution in India, is a cooperative involved in providing milk and milk products. The Academy of Development Science (ADS) in Maharashtra has been involved in the setting up of Grain Banks in different regions. It organises training and capacity-building programmes on food security for NGOs. Its efforts are also directed towards influencing the government's policy on food security. Thus, through these examples, it can be seen that cooperatives are playing an active role in the distribution of food and related items.
final_answer: Thus, through these examples, it can be seen that cooperatives are playing an active role in the distribution of food and related items.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the role of cooperatives in food security and their impact.
